title: Example 17-13: Partial Emphasis Using Mathematical Symbols

illustrates.quote: Mathematical Symbols. Spellers often use mathematical symbols to teach word formation. a. Transcribe all text in word formation “equations” in uncontracted braille. b. If the result of the equation is a complete word, add the contracted form of the word at the end of the equation, enclosed in transcriber’s note indicators. Ignore any print emphasis.

print.notes: A cell-5 heading, then two word-formation equations with partial bold emphasis on the suffixes ('ment', 'ful') in both the equation and its result.
print.printFeatures: Bold on the suffix portion only, in both terms of each equation.
transcriberSupplied: the contracted repeat of each result word in transcriber's note indicators (17.13.1b): @.<amaze;t@.> and @.<hope;l@.> ("amazement", "hopeful")

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille and rule id unchanged. Print's own partial bold on the suffix is NOT re-encoded here: even if marked, Emboss silently drops all typeform from an uncontracted run (F-210), so a bold sub-run and a plain one produce byte-identical output — omitting the bold marking changes nothing observable. The contracted-form annotation at the end of each equation is written here in ordinary parentheses because Emboss has no inline TN segment (F-211, 17.13.1b) — the given braille wraps it in `@.<...@.>`; expect mismatch there. Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).

printCorrections.evidence: references/_gemini/_done/gold-17-A/page-476.png (Example 17-13): print shows "amaze + **ment** = amaze**ment**" and "hope + **ful** = hope**ful**" - bold on the suffix in both places; the gold text had lost the bold although its own notes/printFeatures say "bold on the suffix". The trailing "(amazement)" is the transcriber-supplied contracted repeat in note indicators (17.13.1b), not in the print image; left as it was.

printCorrections.was: items ended with the contracted repeat "(amazement)" and "(hopeful)"
printCorrections.now: items end at the printed result word; the repeats are in print.transcriberSupplied
printCorrections.evidence: references/bana/braille-formats-2016.pdf p.476, rendered at 110 dpi: the print original shows only "amaze + ment = amazement" and "hope + ful = hopeful" (bold on the suffixes). The repeats in transcriber's note indicators are braille-side (17.13.1b).
